audience: evaluator-only; never send this file, group labels, required claims or scores to extraction, qualification or refinement

protocol.sourceBoundary: Evaluate the full original messages and all actual first-extraction items, not a prepared card or a chosen best item. No source asks for extraction or supplies a gold label. Extraction may return nothing; do not force an item or repair the source.
protocol.tupleRule: First decide what the actual selected subject/property/scope/applies/value tuple means. Then judge commitment against that proposition's polarity, conditions and represented claimant. Examples below are meanings, not mandatory wording or a required card count. A tuple about deciding to reject an option may correctly be adopted; the option itself may correctly be rejected. A bare event or report of a decision is not automatically a decision tuple.
protocol.observations: Measurements, reported events, feelings, absence and uncertain causes have unknown decision commitment. Unknown does not permit erasing the meaningful target or its uncertainty. A chosen numeric setting can be adopted. An assistant or user reporting somebody else's explicit choice preserves that represented party's stance, not the reporter's own adoption.
protocol.coverage: Every required claim must survive across the full set of actual cards with meaning, conditions and attribution preserved. One card may cover multiple claims only if its actual representation preserves them separately and commitment is appropriate to its selected tuple; do not demand duplicated cards or exact phrasing. Mixed sources require the observation AND the separate decision. Other supported source details may be extracted, but do not replace required coverage.
protocol.strictSourceSuccess: A source succeeds only with mechanical completion, admission/read/cold verification of every actual card, coverage of ALL required claims, preserved target meaning, and supported commitment on EVERY actual output card, including extras. An unsupported extra cannot be ignored. Report attribution/scope/uncertainty defects separately and fail strict success when they alter required meaning or commitment support. This is a bounded target/commitment test, not full-memory accuracy.
protocol.failures: Keep all 24 sources in both denominators. Empty extraction or any missing required claim fails both arms. Retain/refine all 1–5 actual items at the same indices; invalid output, more than five items, overflow, stage failure and unverifiable cold storage are unresolved source failures in the denominator, never a dropped source or baseline substitution. No retries, repair, replacement or selection of a later attempt; preserve every original attempt.
protocol.itemReporting: Separately report each actual item's tuple match, supported commitment, represented claimant, polarity, uncertainty, conditions, unsupported extras and cold status. Report source-level coverage and paired gains/regressions separately; do not substitute item percentages for the fixed source denominator. Record attribution, scope and uncertainty issues even when they do not change a target/commitment result.
severeErrors: New false adoption of an observation, feeling, uncertain hypothesis, considered option or rejected positive option.
A decision newly assigned to the reporter/user/assistant instead of the source's represented decision maker.
Newly erased uncertainty, negation, material condition, time or scope that turns a claim into a stronger unsupported assertion.
New invented choice, replacement option, factual authority, verified truth, consent or execution permission unsupported by the source.
Any baseline-correct actual decision lost, downgraded, reversed or made unsupported in the candidate, including a correct decision among otherwise failing source cards.

gate.meaning: Diagnostic continuation only; no automatic production promotion or full-core/installed integration claim.

protocol.judging: Two independent masked non-implementing GPT-6.1 Sol raters inspect full sources, required claims and all actual cards. They are from the SAME model family, not human calibration. Preserve every raw judgment and masked mapping. Disagreements require explicit primary source audit with both original judgments and the reason for resolution retained; never silently relabel. Unknown/unresolved judgments block promotion.
protocol.freeze: Primary review and final gate definition precede byte-level SHA256 freeze of source and rubric, private operator, and judging instructions/schema before any paid dispatch. Construct the masked judging packet only afterward from the preserved first actual outputs; preserve its byte hash and mapping. This file authorizes no paid call. Never tune the cohort or rubric against actual outputs.
